meta.title_plain: How Ben Shelton went from quarterback to world No. 4
meta.teaser: Ben Shelton started tennis late, trained with his dad and served his way to No. 4.

page.title: How Ben Shelton went from quarterback to world No. 4
page.bigIdea: Ben Shelton started tennis later than most pros. With his dad as coach, he proved that a late start can still go all the way.

cards.title: A quarterback first
cards.front: Ben was born in 2002 in Atlanta, USA. His first sport wasn't tennis.
cards.back: He played quarterback in American football. Bigger kids kept knocking him down, so around age 12 he started playing tennis regularly, coached by his dad.
cards.tryit: Try 10 overhead throwing motions with no ball. Notice how it feels like a serve.

cards.title: Champion for the Gators
cards.front: Ben's dad, Bryan, was a former pro who coached the Florida Gators.
cards.back: Ben played college tennis for Florida. He clinched the 2021 team title and won the 2022 national singles title. His college record was 65 wins, 10 losses.
cards.tryit: Play a practice set where your only goal is to cheer for one good shot each game.

cards.title: Top 100 without a passport
cards.front: Ben turned pro in 2022, and he rose fast.
cards.back: He won three small 'Challenger' titles in three weeks. That put him in the top 100 before he had ever left the USA.
cards.tryit: Write down three small goals you could reach in three weeks of practice.

cards.title: A serve at 150 mph
cards.front: Ben is a lefty with one of the biggest serves in tennis.
cards.back: He has served at 150 miles per hour (241 km/h). On his first trip abroad, in 2023, he reached the Australian Open quarterfinals.
cards.tryit: Hit 20 serves. Aim 10 wide and 10 down the middle, and count how many land in.

cards.title: Climbing to world No. 4
cards.front: Ben kept improving his whole game, not just his serve.
cards.back: He won big Canadian Open titles in 2025 and 2026. He reached the 2026 US Open final and hit world No. 4 in September 2026.
cards.tryit: Pick one shot besides your serve. Practise it for 15 minutes this week.

words.d: The American football player who throws the ball to start most plays.
The group that runs college sports and championships in the USA.
A smaller pro tournament, one level below the main tour.
A serve so good the other player can't even touch it.
The biggest kind of tournament after the four Grand Slams.

quiz.q: Which sport did Ben play before focusing on tennis?
quiz.hint: Look at card 1. He threw a ball, but not a tennis ball.
quiz.why: He played quarterback, then switched to tennis around age 12.

quiz.q: What was special about Ben reaching the top 100 in 2022?
opts: He had never played outside the USA
He did it in his first week
quiz.hint: Think about what a passport is for.
quiz.why: He won three Challenger titles in the USA and broke into the top 100 before ever going abroad.

quiz.q: Who has coached Ben in college and on the pro tour?
quiz.hint: He was a former pro who coached the Florida Gators.
quiz.why: Bryan Shelton coached Ben at Florida and later left the job to travel with him on tour.

quiz.q: Why did Ben keep working on more than his serve?
opts: Serves are not allowed to be fast
A great player needs strong shots in long rallies too
quiz.hint: Read card 5. Big serves win points, but not every point.
quiz.why: Building a fuller game helped him win titles on every surface and reach No. 4.

page.think: Ben started tennis late, but his football throwing helped his serve. What skill from another game or hobby of yours could help your tennis?
tries: Do 10 shadow serves each day, copying a smooth throwing motion
Watch highlights of Ben Shelton's serve and notice how he uses his legs
Play one practice set where you come to the net at least 5 times
Tell Dad one idea from this report
